findings.summary: crates/athena-core/src/run/close.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: A revert record with exit code 0 leaks into the job-wide `ran` list through the unchanged filter line, which bypasses the per-criterion scope.
findings.evidence: verify.rs 378 keeps `.filter(|c| c.passed && (c.exit_code == Some(0) || (c.reused && c.exit_code.is_none())))` and adds every match's command to `ran`, which every criterion uses (line 503). Decision 3 and step 3 set passed = true on every revert record. A demonstration that still passes without the fix exits 0 (run/tests.rs 3164-3186 has that case: 'exit code 0', 'passed without the fix'). Such a record matches the filter, so its command becomes seen for every behavior criterion, including ones outside revert_for. It is also a run on the reverted copy, not the candidate tree. Demonstration case (e) uses only a failing run, so it would not catch this. Fix: Keep revert records out of the job-wide loop without editing the searched text. For example, chain `.filter(|c| c.revert_for.is_empty())` before the existing filter call, so the line `c.reused && c.exit_code.is_none()` stays the same. Add a verify.rs test: a revert record with exit_code Some(0) and revert_for [3], cited by criterion 2, stays unseen with the Major finding. Say in the docs whether an exit-0 revert run counts for its own criteria at all.

findings.summary: The run-level 'criterion citing the record is met' assertion has no seam for making the fake verifier cite the record.
findings.evidence: run_demonstration_job(repo, plan, runs, also_edit) builds its script from planning_script plus a producer edit hook. No parameter controls the verifier's structured output or its cited commands, and the plan does not say how the fake verifier will cite 'fails-without-1'. Fix: Name the seam: add a parameter or a variant of run_demonstration_job that overrides the Role::Verifier turn's criteria commands with the record's command or name. Then assert that the stored criterion is met with commands_verified true.

findings.summary: The record's name is built in two places.
findings.evidence: run/checks.rs 331 already builds `fails-without-{first criterion}` for the CheckSpec, and revert_record builds the name again from group.criteria. Fix: Take the name from `run.name`, which run_check copies from the spec, or have both places call one helper, so the shown name and the recorded name cannot drift apart.

summary: I read verify.rs judge() (lines 362-509), run/checks.rs (demonstration_records and demonstration_runs, 215-355), run/verification.rs (64-140), close.rs landing_body, the admission filter-line test, and the run-level demonstration helper. I also grepped the readers of `.checks`. The design mostly holds up and fits one producer run: the `revert_for` scope field, the per-criterion rule, adding the records after the verifier's inputs are built, the close.rs count helper and the carried-line rendering. One soundness hole is left. Every revert record has passed = true, and the plan keeps the job-wide filter at verify.rs 378 (`c.passed && (c.exit_code == Some(0) || ...)`) exactly as it is. So a revert run that exits 0 (the test still passed without the fix, a case the existing test a_demonstration_that_still_passes_without_the_fix_is_recorded_as_passing produces) goes into the job-wide `ran` list and counts for every criterion. That breaks the plan's own per-criterion scope and adds to the D43 loosening. None of the planned negative cases uses exit 0, so no test would catch it. Everything else I checked is right: the helpers exist, the dependents list covers the `.checks` readers I found, and Athena's close.rs finding is answered with a reason. One small gap: the run-level verdict assertion needs the fake verifier to cite the record, and run_demonstration_job has no parameter for that.
